notes: Found the cheapest roses on Amazon in five minutes, checked out in the user's own browser on approval, and verified the order number on the orders page.
Drafts replies and waits for a yes, and twice corrected its own earlier claims unprompted, once on an order number and once on a date.
Carried the order number and delivery date across days and tied them to the calendar, though it treated the recipient as a different person.
Warned the flowers would land while the user was away, checked proposed meeting times against a flight, and flagged a stuck deposit email with bank details.
Named a vegan spot a block away plus three alternatives with ratings, price range and hours, and noticed the user was out of town first.
Found Friday tables, recovered from its own browser when the user's went offline, and confirmed no deposit before stopping at the phone field.
Found the cheapest nonstop round trip and reached the airline's passenger page, spelling out the basic economy and return airport catches.
Never types the user's card or birthday, stops before every confirm step, and stripped names, amounts and order numbers from a public profile.
Reads Gmail and calendar, shops through a paired browser and syncs wearables, but has no plain HTTP tool, so API-only integrations are out.
Has no outbound calling; it hands over the business's number for the user to call.
